mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the monetary policy environment supports risk-taking.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0 (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST > 1700 and RSAFS > 650000) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy expands.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances when both HOUST > 1700 and RSAFS > 650000 (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in less than 40% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate profits fall.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS > 150000) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) signal a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending rises.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 3.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) consistently indicates expanding manufacturing activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when INDPRO is rising (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Higher retail sales (RSAFS) directly reflect increased consumer spending, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when RSAFS is rising (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).
